The Fed's job is really to take care of the inflation piece of it. We are all absolutely committed to getting inflation back down to 2%, but long run, it's going to be fundamentals of debt issuance, of investment, of economic growth and productivity. Long run, that's what sets the Treasury yields, and not just in the U.S. but government bond yields all around the world.
MARGARET BRENNAN: No, and I appreciate as a central banker, you don't want to get involved in fiscal policy or what the markets are doing day to day, but there is this debate right now about whether something more fundamental is shifting. Investor Mohamed El-Erian wrote in the New York Times, "There's a breathtaking leap in the cost of borrowing. If it persists, it could mark the beginning of a structural economic shift more enduring and more globally consequential than most previous episodes of market volatility." Is that overstating things? Are we in the midst of a huge shift?
: Well, there are a lot of different factors going on at the same time. So, the stock market, as you know, has been really bullish for the last several years, really excited about AI and the prospects that that will lead to productivity growth. You know, a more optimistic take on these market moves is that the bond market is catching up to the stock market, and the bond market is seeing a higher growth trajectory. If the- if the global economy is in for higher productivity growth and higher growth, you would also expect to see higher yields all around the world. Now, I'm not endorsing that view. I'm not saying that's right. But, there are many different ways that you could see bond yields go up globally. It is- Mr. El-Erian is right. These moves are happening all around the world at the same time. I think that there are negative views of what could be driving that. There are also more optimistic views. It's hard to know right now which is the- the bigger driver.
MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, the vice president J.D. Vance, in a TV interview, said Secretary Bessent has a, quote, "very discreet plan to shrink the nation's debt." Mr. Bessent is holding a press conference tomorrow, or is supposed to, and- and he said he's going to do things about fiscal consolidation. What are the things that people at home should be listening for that say America's debt load is really being dealt with now, that this isn't a problem?
: Well, I just think you can look to the Congressional Budget Office, which makes forecasts of debt, U.S. debt and deficits for decades out into the future, and many Fed leaders have said for a long time that the debt trajectory is on an unsustainable path. I think ultimately it's up to our fiscal actors. That's the Treasury and the executive branch working with Congress to design a fiscal package that can change that and put it on a sustainable path. But obviously, you know, you said it a moment ago. That's not the Fed's role. The Fed's role is to take whatever they decide to do, put that into our forecast of the economy, and then our job is to take that and get inflation back down to our 2% target and achieve our dual mandate goals. And my colleagues and I are all committed to doing so.
MARGARET BRENNAN: Right. And you have a meeting at the end of this week, I understand, out in Jackson Hole. But, I'm- I'm wondering how all these dots connect because do you think that this kind of activity and level of concern in the markets is going to make your job harder when it comes to- to making some decisions or cause the Fed to intervene?
: I don't think so, right. As I mentioned a few moments ago, there's every indication that the U.S. Treasury market is functioning as it should--
MARGARET BRENNAN: Okay.
: --that trades are taking place. That there's liquidity in the market, and so that enables us to focus on the federal funds rate as our primary policy tool to get inflation back down. And so I think we have the freedom to do what we need to do to achieve our goals that Congress has assigned us.
MARGARET BRENNAN: Okay. At that last Fed meeting that was held, you dissented from the broader decision to hold interest rates steady. You said there have now been five years of persistently high inflation, and, sort of like, let's get on with it was my understanding. You were saying let's start to possibly raise rates. You mentioned a quarter of a percentage point. Are you still thinking that that's necessary next month?
: Well, I want to get- more data has yet to come between now and our next FOMC meeting, so I don't want to prejudge things. But what's happening in the Middle East, the conflict with Iran, is now a big driver of what's happening on inflation because, as you know, energy goes into every facet of the U.S. economy, and the longer that conflict, the more turmoil there is. The longer it goes on, the bigger effect it ends up having on the U.S. economy and on inflation. And even if it's driven by geopolitical factors like that, ultimately it does affect inflation. Ultimately, it does have a bearing on the Federal Reserve's mandate and so the longer that goes on, the less confident I am that inflation is going to return to target. You know, for- for five years we've been saying inflation is going to return to target in the next year or two. It just keeps getting pushed out. Eventually, we're going to have to do more. And I'm not sure if we're there yet, we need to see more data. But I don't want to prejudge the next meeting. But I'm not feeling confident right now that inflation is heading back down to target in a short period of time.
MARGARET BRENNAN: And- and we should say that at that press conference, Secretary Bessent is expected to have tomorrow, he's supposed to talk about switching to financial warfare, or I guess returning to where we were and maybe ratcheting it up with financial warfare against Iran. It seems that that's the foot forward rather than military conflict. Does that change anything for you?
: I- I- it's too soon--
MARGARET BRENNAN: Okay.
: --to know. I don't know what the secretary will announce, and I don't know what the implication will be for--
MARGARET BRENNAN: Yeah.
: --energy prices and commodity prices.
MARGARET BRENNAN: Yeah. Let me ask you as well about what we heard in the last few days about the trade tension with Canada. You are in Minnesota, key border state there. Prime Minister Carney said there will be new retaliatory tariffs rolling out next week on steel, dairy appliances, ag equipment, pulp and paper, electronics. You've got a lot of cross-border trade here. Do you have any indication how significant the impact will be?
: Well, Canada is an important trading partner for America. You know, we talked about the five years of elevated inflation that has largely been driven by what we call supply shocks. One of those supply shocks is the trade and tariff conflicts. And so to the extent that we can get to a new- a new normal, a- a- a level of- whatever the trade dynamic is going to be, once we can get to that steady state, then businesses can adjust, and the inflationary impact can fade into the background. The longer there's back and forth on the trade front, just like the longer there's back and forth in the conflict of Iran, the imprint in inflation end up being extended and delayed, and so that's another factor to pay close- close attention to.
MARGARET BRENNAN: Right. Well, we will follow that, and we appreciate your insight as always. Neel Kashkari, thanks for joining us this morning. Face Nation will be right back.

"We survived Assad, but not Al-Sharaa": forced closure silences Syrian news outlet "Hashtag"
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:58:05 UTC
01:58:05 KST

ALBAWABA - The independent Syrian news outlet **Hashtag Syria** said it was closing after 12 years, citing increasing pressure, restrictions and threats against its journalists that made working from within Syria too dangerous.
The closure was not due to financial problems or falling readership, but rather a hostile climate for independent journalism that “grew increasingly hostile,” Hashtag said in a lengthy statement posted on August 23.
The outlet directly accused Syria’s Ministry of Information and the officials overseeing the media sector of having essentially driven an independent Syrian news organization out of the country.
Hashtag was created under Syria’s 2011 media law and was active during the administration of former President Bashar al-Assad. It said its journalists had investigated sensitive issues from corruption and oil smuggling to telecommunications, aviation and networks of political and economic influence.
Its staff, said the organization, had received death threats, legal action and security pressure over the years.
Hashtag said it hoped the shifting political landscape in Syria would allow more room for independent journalism after the fall of the Assad government on December 8, 2024.
The outlet, instead, says it got caught up in a fight over its licensing status.
Hashtag was banned from operating inside Syria in March 2026, over what authorities reportedly called incomplete licensing procedures. The outlet dismissed the explanation, stating it had submitted the required documents and was pursuing legal avenues to address the matter.
Hashtag officials later described the organization as “not cooperative,” a characterization it strongly denied.
“What does it mean for a media organization to be ‘cooperative’ with the Ministry of Information?” asked the outlet, arguing journalists should be scrutinizing authorities, not seeking their approval.
The pressure “shrank the team at Hashtag from about 20 journalists to six volunteers,” the company said. Some staff were targeted with smear campaigns, threats and attempted arrests, the outlet said.
Hashtag said it could move its operations overseas but had opted not to, arguing that a Syrian news organization should be able to operate from inside Syria.
The outlet announced its suspension but said it would continue to pursue legal action and preserve documents tied to the alleged threats and restrictions.
It finished its statement: “Hashtag will end today, but the questions it posed will not.”

Landfill collapse kills at least 30 in Guinea as rescuers search for survivors
Heavy rains washed over waste at a landfill in Guinea’s capital Conakry on Sunday, triggering a landslide that buried nearby shacks
A landslide at a landfill in Guinea’s capital killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted the collapse of a massive mound of waste that engulfed nearby tents and shacks.
The incident happened less than a week after the government announced plans to close the site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the continuing rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa.
The landslide took place at around 2am local time in the Gbessia commune of Conakry, according to a government statement.
The death toll was 30, with six people seriously injured and 16 more lightly injured, the statement said.
Rescuers were using excavators and other tools to clear the site of the landslide, which witnesses said was large enough to bury a block of flats along with more precarious dwellings.
One woman, Cire Diallo, told reporters at the scene that her five children were killed. “I have lost all my children. All I can do is put my trust in God,” she said.

‘Spider-Man’ tops box office in fourth weekend; ‘The Odyssey’ becomes Nolan’s highest-grossing film
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:53:02 UTC
01:53:02 KST

‘Spider-Man’ tops box office in fourth weekend; ‘The Odyssey’ becomes Nolan’s highest-grossing film
“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” fought off a slew of newcomers, including a comedy, a horror franchise, a Jason Statham action movie and a family pic, to maintain its first-place spot at the box office in its fourth weekend in theaters. “The Odyssey” also became Christopher Nolan’s highest grossing movie ever, both domestically and internationally.
For the year, “The Odyssey” is second only to “Spider-Man,” which added $39 million from 4,006 theaters in the U.S. and Canada, according to studio estimates Sunday. “Spider-Man,” which has now made over $854.9 million in North America, will soon surpass “Avengers: Endgame” to become the second highest-grossing domestic release of all time. The record holder is currently “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($936.7 million).
Sony also had the second biggest movie of the weekend with “Insidious: Out of the Further.” The sixth movie in the franchise, produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster, made $25.3 million from 3,303 theaters. Internationally, it made $35 million. Its $18 million production budget makes it the most expensive movie of the series.
Third place went to “The Odyssey,” which earlier this week became the highest grossing R-rated movie of all time, surpassing “Deadpool & Wolverine.” It added $19.5 million in its sixth weekend in North American theaters, where it continues to play in over 3,000 locations, bringing its domestic total to just under $539.1 million. That pushes it past the $534.9 million from “The Dark Knight” — a previous high-water mark for Nolan — not accounting for inflation. Internationally, it added $68 million, driven largely by China and Korea, which brings its worldwide total to $1.4 billion.
The other big newcomers landed further down the charts. “Mutiny,” starring Statham as a man wrongly accused of murdering his billionaire boss, opened in sixth place with $7.5 million from 2,703 locations. The Lionsgate release (an acquisition) was intended to be a theatrical only release, but a few days before it opened it was accidentally available for free on Prime Video for a few hours before the mistake was remedied. The glitch might have impacted its opening weekend earnings, but the film also had some fairly bad reviews working against it.
Even more poorly reviewed was “Spa Weekend,” a girl’s trip comedy from the men behind “The Hangover” and “Bad Moms,” starring Isla Fisher, Leslie Mann, Anna Faris and Michelle Buteau. It made an estimated $3.1 million in 2,009 locations. Women accounted for some 84% of opening weekend ticket buyers, according to PostTrak. The 25th anniversary re-release of “The Fast and the Furious” made slightly more.
“The Magic Faraway Tree,” starring Andrew Garfield, opened outside of the top 10 with $1.4 million from 1,611 screens.
The young Anthony Bourdain movie “Tony” continues to do quite well, however, earning $5 million from 1,652 screens.
The summer season, which runs through Labor Day, has now generated an estimated $4.4 billion in ticket sales in North America, putting it among the top four highest grossing summers ever.
“We’re in the home stretch of what I think will go down in box office history as maybe one of the most key and pivotal summer movie seasons ever,” said Paul Dergarabedian, the head of marketplace trends for Rentrak. “I don’t know how you can replicate this summer. Studios will try.”
Michael O’Leary, the president and CEO of the movie theater trade organization Cinema United, noted the wide variety of movies in the marketplace that have helped contribute to a big summer. Part of that, he told The Associated Press, was that the industry pipeline is finally bouncing back from the effects of the Hollywood strikes in 2023.
“The thing that I’m most excited about, frankly, is just the enthusiasm of moviegoers,” O’Leary said. “You feel it when you go to the theater. There’s an energy about being in the theater that hasn’t been there in the recent past.”
The year overall has also surpassed $7 billion, which is up about 20.4% from 2025, but about 7.1% behind 2019.
Top 10 movies by domestic box office
With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak:
1. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $39 million.
2. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” $25.3 million.
3. “The Odyssey,” $19.5 million.
4. “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,” $9.1 million.
5. “The End of Oak Street,” $9 million.
6. “Mutiny,” $7.5 million.
7. “Tony,” $5 million.
8. “The Fast and the Furious” (25th anniversary re-release), $3.1 million.
9. “Spa Weekend,” $3.1 million.
10. “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” $1.9 million.

Reigning NFL rushing champion James Cook is underpaid but he’s focused on helping the Bills win
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:53:02 UTC

Reigning NFL rushing champion James Cook is underpaid but he’s focused on helping the Bills win
James Cook got a new contract last year and backed it up by leading the NFL is rushing.
Now, he’s underpaid.
The Buffalo Bills gave Cook a $46 million, four-year deal that’s a bargain compared to the money teams handed out to running backs this month.
He’s not complaining. At least, not publicly.
Buffalo Bills running back James Cook joins On Football with Rob Maaddi and talks about being suddenly underpaid but focused on helping the Bills win.
“Just keep growing, just keep elevating my game, be the best version of me,” Cook said on the AP’s “On Football” podcast. “Each and every day I step on the field, sky’s the limit.”
Jahmyr Gibbs became the highest-paid running back in NFL history when the Detroit Lions signed him to a $67.5 million, three-year contract with $51.5 million guaranteed and an average annual salary of $22.5 million.
Bijan Robinson received a $66.75 million, three-year deal from the Atlanta Falcons with $51.6 million guaranteed, and an average annual salary of $22.25 million.
The Indianapolis Colts gave Jonathan Taylor a $44 million, two-year deal.
Those contracts set a new bar for running backs, surpassing Saquon Barkley ($20.6 million annually) and Christian McCaffrey ($19 million annually).
Still, running backs are underpaid compared to wide receivers. Twenty-five receivers are making more money per season than Gibbs and Robinson. That includes Robinson’s teammate, Drake London. Robinson led the NFL last year in scrimmage yards with 2,298. London was 50th with 919 yards. But he’s making $13 million more per season.
After the season, running backs could make this an issue like they did a few years ago when they met virtually to discuss their contracts.
For now, it’s all business.
Cook is focused on trying to help the Bills get to an elusive Super Bowl victory.
Led by Josh Allen, Buffalo has won a playoff game in each of the past six seasons but hasn’t made it past the AFC championship game.
“We don’t have to do nothing but keep being us man, and just get over that hump,” Cook said. “The ultimate goal is to win the Super Bowl, but you got to take day by day and step by step to get there. It ain’t gonna be easy. So we know that and each and every day, each and every week we step on the field, we’re trying to put our best foot forward to win.”
A frustrating loss to Denver in overtime in the divisional round last season cost coach Sean McDermott his job. Offensive coordinator Joe Brady was promoted to take his place so Allen, Cook and Co. will run the same system.
“Joe is going to be Joe,” Cook said. “He’s gonna let us be, let us have fun, but also be business as usual. So, I don’t think nothing changed, man. It’s just the same, it’s just us, man. But we got to do the little things different to get over that hump. And, I mean, we’ve been doing it, we’ve been working our tail off, and it’s going to show on Sundays.”
Cook ran for a career-best 1,621 yards and 12 touchdowns last season, earning his third straight Pro Bowl appearance and making the second team AP All-Pro team.

CONAKRY, Guinea (AP) — A mountainous heap of refuse collapsed at the largest landfill in Guinea ‘s capital of Conakry early on Sunday, killing 30 people, according to the central government.
Authorities said that heavy rains, which started at around 2 a.m., washed over the refuse at Dar Es Salam — the largest landfill in Conakry — and triggered a landslide that buried nearby shacks. A search and rescue operation was underway to find survivors. Six people were seriously injured and several homes were destroyed.
The site, an open-air waste dump which is the largest in the city, had been designated for closure on Sunday, according to Lt. Col. Baldé Mamadou Bailo, the sanitation officer for the military engineering battalion.
Locals living around the landfill had been given eviction notices, which forced many to leave the area, but many others were still around at the time of the disaster, according to authorities.
“We will ensure that the remaining families are relocated elsewhere,” Dienabou Touré, the minister of territorial administration and decentralization, said at the scene.
Guinea is mineral-rich with huge deposits of bauxite — the largest in the world — and also has iron ore, gold, diamonds and minerals. However, according to the World Bank, 43.7% of the population lives below the national poverty line.

Gaza border residents warn: Today it’s kites, tomorrow explosive drones
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:52:50 UTC
01:52:50 KST

“This is not just about a kite, but about normalizing the situation,” Bar Manshuri, head of security for the Sha’ar HaNegev Regional Council, said Sunday.
Seven kites launched from the direction of the Gaza Strip have been found in communities near the border over the past two weeks, and residents say they recognize the same pattern that preceded the wave of incendiary-kite attacks in 2018. “It’s not the colorful kites that worry us, it’s the process,” one resident said.
Another kite was found Sunday morning in agricultural fields near Kibbutz Kfar Aza, close to the Black Arrow memorial. Four others were found over the weekend in the Nahal Oz area. No incendiary or explosive materials were found attached to the kites, which authorities believe were launched from the northern Gaza Strip. Initial examinations in the field indicate that children and teenagers were flying the kites, according to the assessment cited in the report, with the activity believed to have been directed by Hamas commanders.
Manshuri said the incidents must be treated as an early warning rather than dismissed because the kites currently carry no explosives. “We need to identify the event, respond to it and understand that it also has an impact on residents’ resilience,” she said.
“Residents of Kfar Aza are only now beginning to return home, and from our perspective this is not just a kite. We need to look at what the next steps could be, which is why we are raising the flag now. As the saying goes, the writing is on the wall. Now the writing is in the sky.”
She called for clearer and more proactive security measures. “The biggest danger is that this will become normalized because there is no incendiary or explosive material attached to the kites,” Manshuri said.
“We have to make sure we are not surprised because we thought a kite with nothing attached was just children playing. The military and the state cannot normalize this. You cannot tell us, ‘It will be fine,’ or ‘We have it under control.’ Not after October 7. It significantly damages public trust.”
Manshuri warned that failure to respond now could lead to a familiar escalation pattern. “If there is no solution, the next thing will be an incendiary kite, then explosive balloons and after that drones, including drones carrying explosives,” she said. “We want to stop this on our terms, not according to Hamas’ timetable.”
She said residents appreciate the IDF and security forces operating in the area, but argued that policy must remain offensive and proactive rather than reactive. “It is important that we do not assume that because we control 60% of the Strip, everything is fine and calm,” she said. “We always have to think one step ahead.”
Manshuri also stressed the need to maintain local defense capabilities as residents return to Gaza-border communities. “In the end, those who responded to the attacks were the local defense squads, community security coordinators and their deputies,” she said.
“We want to make sure every community has a trained and armed force. Their job is ultimately to protect the communities from every security threat. That requires personnel, training and drills. It is important to preserve readiness and not reduce manpower. We always have to think about the next threat.”
She added that public confidence depends on the state responding even to seemingly minor incidents. “It is important that the public believe the state and everyone responsible for the security of Gaza-border residents will do everything necessary to protect them,” she said. “A small incident requires a response. We do not want to wait for a large, uncontrolled event that causes serious harm.”
The Israel Gaza Envelope Forum, which represents residents of communities near the Strip, said residents are less concerned about the kites themselves than about what it described as an approach of containment.
“Residents of the Gaza border are not worried about the kites, but about IDF statements that reflect the old containment mindset: ‘These are children, there are no explosives attached, we are monitoring it,’” the forum said.
“Hamas will keep adjusting to the IDF’s pace because there is no mechanism stopping it, exactly as happened before the massacre.”

Adel Abdelrheem and Rania Abushamala
23 August 2026•Update: 23 August 2026
 Flash floods have displaced 63 families and damaged 130 homes in South Kordofan and North Darfur in southern and western Sudan, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday.
In a statement, the organization said heavy rains and flash floods ravaged the village of Al-Atafa in the Al-Tadamon locality of South Kordofan, displacing 49 families, destroying 49 homes and partially damaging 38 others.
The UN agency said the displaced families sought refuge in temporary shelters located in open areas within the same locality.
The IOM said that rains and floods also displaced 14 families in the Kabkabiya locality of North Darfur state on Thursday.
According to the organization, 14 homes were destroyed and 29 shelters partially damaged in the area.
There was no immediate comment from the Sudanese authorities on the report.
Sudan experiences heavy rainfall during its rainy season, which runs from June to October, often resulting in widespread annual flooding.
These natural disasters come as Sudan has been gripped by a war between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023, leaving tens of thousands dead and displacing around 13 million people, according to UN and international estimates.

UK pro-Palestine groups reject 'bizarre' China funding allegations
UK campaigners have rejected allegations that China is providing covert support to pro-Palestine marches and activities, calling them part of a wider campaign to delegitimise protests against Israel.
Right-wing and pro-Israel media have over the past week suggested that Beijing is providing secret funding to the protests after The Telegraph published claims made by US lawmakers investigating Code Pink's activities in the UK.
The allegations of Chinese involvement originate from dubious claims that an American businessman accused of having ties to China made payments to a UK-based company linked to the American activist group.
The Home Office is reportedly examining the allegations after several MPs and newspapers demanded an investigation.
The Stop the War Coalition said claims that China has been funding the UK pro-Palestine movement were "bizarre and completely without foundation".
"The pro-Palestine marches organised by the Palestine Coalition in the UK are funded entirely by money donated by the members and affiliates of the six coalition organisations, of which Code Pink, a US-based group, is not one," a spokesperson told The New Arab.
Code Pink has participated in some of the pro-Palestine marches in the UK, which have drawn hundreds of thousands of people to rally against the Gaza genocide and Israel's other wars across the region.
However, it is not among the organisers of the major national rallies in London, which are convened by the six organisations in the Palestine Coalition, which include the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Stop the War, and Friends of Al-Aqsa.
The allegations centre around the activities of Neville Roy Singham, who is under investigation by the US House of Representatives Ways and Means Committee and the US justice department for allegedly supporting "pro-Hamas, pro-communist causes".
Singham, the husband of Code Pink co-founder Jodie Evans, has been accused for years of promoting China's viewpoint internationally. In 2023 he was the subject of a New York Times investigation that detailed his funding of progressive causes abroad and alleged ties to Chinese state media.
Congressional sources told The Telegraph that they are investigating a series of payments worth £260,000 which they say were made by organisations linked to Singham between 2020 and 2024 to an unidentified British company that is said to be affiliated to Code Pink.
No evidence of Chinese state funding to either Singham or Code Pink was provided, while the nature of the relationship between Singham and the unidentified companies was not disclosed.
A Code Pink spokesperson denied taking money from any foreign government when approached for comment by The New Arab.
"We are not funded by billionaires but by individual donors and through administrative grants for non-profits, and we operate without influence or support from any foreign entity," they said.
The US justice department did not respond to a request for comment.
The claims have fuelled demands for the government to investigate alleged Chinese involvement in the protests, including by MPs from the Labour and Conservative parties.
Alicia Kearns, a Conservative MP who recently chaired the Foreign Affairs Select Committee, called for an urgent investigation and for the government to "use the full force of the National Security Act" against groups she said aim to "spread sedition and undermine our democracy".
Stop the War said the allegations were another attempt to discredit the pro-Palestine movement.
"This latest, spurious claim is yet another desperate attempt by the establishment to de-legitimise our movement, at a time when public opinion in Britain is overwhelmingly opposed to Israel's military actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon," it told The New Arab.
Since October 2023, right-wing politicians and commentators have portrayed the rallies as antisemitic "hate marches" and pushed for a total ban on pro-Palestine activism.
The Labour government has mounted a crackdown on Palestinian activism, imposing stricter conditions on protests and proscribing Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation.
Ismail Patel, chair of Friends of Al-Aqsa, described the accusations as part of a broader "McCarthyist" campaign aimed at ending pro-Palestine protests.
"We have been told these marches were Islamist, then pro-Hamas, then antisemitic, now communist," he told The New Arab.
"The accusation keeps changing because the accusation was never the point. The point is the assumption beneath it: that British Muslims and young people are incapable of independent moral judgement and must be taking instructions from abroad."

Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull in damp conditions at the banked final corner before hitting the barriers heavily, bringing out the red flag. The Dutch driver emerged unhurt from the accident.
Pole-sitter Norris led at the original start, while Antonelli passed Mercedes teammate Russell for second.

Norris remained close to Antonelli as the pair pulled away at the front, with changing conditions and pit-stop strategy shaping the race.
The British driver made his final stop for hard tires on Lap 48 and rejoined in third place behind Lewis Hamilton and Antonelli.
Norris overtook Antonelli around the outside at Tarzan corner on Lap 54, narrowly avoiding Hamilton as he completed the move.
Esteban Ocon then stopped on track on Lap 55, prompting a virtual safety car.
Hamilton pitted one lap later, allowing Norris to regain the lead, while Antonelli subsequently made another stop before recovering to finish second.
Norris controlled the closing stages and crossed the line 11.536 seconds ahead of Antonelli to secure his second consecutive Grand Prix victory.
Russell completed the podium after resisting late pressure from Ferrari drivers Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
Hamilton challenged Russell for third on the final lap, with Leclerc also close behind, but the Mercedes driver held his position to finish ahead of the Ferrari pair.
Antonelli’s runner-up finish took him to 242 points and extended his Drivers’ Championship lead to 59 points over Hamilton and Russell, who are tied on 183.

Ladakh seeks Centre's approval for 36 check dams to expand irrigation

Ladakh seeks Centre's approval for 36 check dams to expand irrigation
Edited by: Rohitashwa Ranjan / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 23, 2026, 22:16 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
While Ladakh is endowed with abundant glacier and snowmelt resources, vast stretches of its cultivable land have historically faced acute irrigation shortages.
NEW DELHI: The Ladakh administration on Sunday submitted a proposal to the Union ministry of Jal Shakti for the construction of 36 check dams to strengthen water availability and expand irrigation potential in the Union Territory.The proposal includes seven Himalayan rock check dams in Leh and 29 reinforced cement concrete (RCC) check dams in Kargil, at an estimated cost of more than Rs 56 crore.A Lok Bhavan spokesperson said the proposal has been submitted for inclusion under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) and is awaiting consideration and approval from the ministry.According to the detailed project report submitted to the Jal Shakti ministry, the proposed check dams are expected to irrigate more than 18,600 acres of land.The administration said the initiative is aimed at conserving water and improving its availability for agriculture in Ladakh, where water scarcity remains a major challenge during the agricultural season despite the region's glaciers, snowfall and glacial meltwater.Currently, less than one percent of the total annual snow and glacial meltwater is utilised, the spokesperson said.The proposed check dams will also create an average storage capacity of 25-30 million litres of water in shallow stretches of rivers.
The administration said such structures have shown durability and resistance to increasing water flows.Ladakh lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena said that recent initiatives, including the diversion of around 90 million litres of glacier water from Stok Nallah into the Igoo-Phey Canal and Chushot village canal, demonstrated how simple, cost-effective and environmentally suitable interventions could improve water availability and agriculture.
"The rock check dams and recent initiative to divert approximately 90 million litres of glacier water from Stok Nallah into Igoo-Phey Canal and Chushot village canal demonstrates that simple, cost-effective and environmentally suitable interventions can make a transformative difference to water availability and agriculture," the LG said."We must harness every possible water resource and create a water-secure, agriculturally prosperous and climate-resilient Ladakh," he added.

Germany’s AfD eyes Saxony-Anhalt win as first step toward federal power

Germany’s AfD eyes Saxony-Anhalt win as first step toward federal power
BERLIN - Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is banking on a breakthrough in September’s state election to build momentum for a future national victory, the party’s co-leader Alice Weidel said on Aug 23.
“We will form the government in Saxony-Anhalt,” Weidel said in an interview with public broadcaster ZDF, referring to the eastern German state that votes on Sept 6.
While the party’s lead candidate in the state has stated the AfD’s aim to govern alone there, Weidel went further, expressing confidence the party will secure the necessary majority to govern in the state alone.
A recent Infratest dimap poll shows AfD with 41 per cent support, well ahead of 24 per cent for Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservative Christian Democrats CDU.
Despite its strong showing in some past regional elections, AfD has yet to enter a state or federal government because all other major parties have ruled out cooperation with it.
Weidel said the CDU’s refusal to work with the AfD — a policy known in Germany as the “firewall” — was weakening the conservatives and would eventually put her party in a position to govern nationally.
“The CDU will never win another federal election,” she said.
The AfD has long argued that the “firewall” was undemocratic, while the CDU says the policy is necessary because AfD poses a threat to Germany’s fundamental principles and its constitutional order.
The AfD also leads national voting-intention polls, though with a smaller margin. The latest Politbarometer survey by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen put the party at 27 per cent, compared with 22 per cent for the CDU/CSU bloc.
Saxony-Anhalt is the first of three state elections in September. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania vote on Sept 20.
Weidel has also repeated the party’s call for a tougher immigration policy and Germany’s withdrawal from the European system of passport-free travel to better secure its borders. REUTERS

Nausėda assures Ukraine of continued military and EU integration support
Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said this following the Ukraine–Nordic-Baltic Eight (NB8) summit in Kyiv on August 23, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
“For Lithuania, it is very important to remain consistent. We signed an agreement on my country’s annual support, which will be no less than 0.25% of our GDP each year. I cannot let you down, Mr. President, and Lithuanians cannot let Ukrainians down. Therefore, we will spend at least 0.25% every year in various forms. But first and foremost, we will help you strengthen your air defense and the purchase ammunition,” Nausėda said.
He also expressed gratitude to Ukraine for its experience in modern warfare. This, the politician noted, is very important for countries that are vulnerable and exposed to various forms of hybrid attacks.
Nausėda recalled that his country is located next to two adversaries — Belarus and Russia — and understands very well what daily pressure in various forms means, including illegal migration and the appearance of various drones or weather balloons.
“So together with you, with your help and support, we are better prepared to meet all these challenges, confront them, and deal with them much more successfully,” the Lithuanian president stressed.
He also placed particular emphasis on his “special attitude” toward Ukraine’s integration into the European Union.
“This is a very important element of your security guarantees, because I call integration into the European Union a long-term security guarantee for Ukraine,” Nausėda said.
He said it was very important for Ukraine to fulfill its commitments, implement reforms, accelerate the reform process, achieve the so-called “interim benchmarks,” and demonstrate results, particularly to skeptics in the EU who are not particularly supportive of further enlargement.” It is also important to demonstrate a shared understanding of reforms among the political elite and society and overcome the “certain hesitancy” of some EU members, he stressed.

Bilingual education
I am writing regarding the article titled “Basic misunderstanding of EMI” (Aug. 9, page 8).
Although I agree with much of what Jye Smallwood says about the problems with English-medium instruction at the university level, the issue begins earlier.
If Taiwan wants to become a bilingual nation, English education needs to start from preschool and continue throughout a child’s education. Children are like sponges when they are young. They need to be exposed to English regularly and be given the opportunity to use it.
This does not mean replacing Mandarin with English. In Canada, specifically in Ontario’s French-immersion system, children can receive a large amount of instruction in a second language while continuing to learn and use their primary language.
By the time Taiwanese students reach university, they should already have many years of experience using English.
Taiwan has a surplus of English teachers with bachelor’s degrees and TEFL qualifications. Many might not have formal teaching credentials required by some schools, but they already have English ability and classroom experience. Why not use these teachers and give them additional training to bring them up to the required standard?
Taiwan would gain a larger pool of English teachers to help build its bilingual education system, while these teachers would gain better qualifications and more opportunities.
Many foreign teachers who do not have deep roots or responsibilities in Taiwan might leave for better opportunities in South Korea, China or the Middle East. Once these teachers leave Taiwan, it could be harder to attract them back.
If Taiwan is serious about becoming a bilingual nation, it needs to stop trying to initiate the teaching when students reach university. The solution must begin when children are young and continue throughout their education.
Taiwan should build a system that produces students who can speak English confidently while remaining fully capable in Mandarin. Otherwise, Bilingual 2030 would remain more of a goal than a reality.
Paul Garrelfs
Toronto, Canada

Photo: Wang Mei-hsiu, Taipei Times

BOOKMAN BILINGUAL 雙語書林： Chinglish or Natural English? 中式英語或道地英語？
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:47 UTC
01:38:47 KST

1. 他找到他追求的志業了嗎？
ˇ Has he found his calling?
χ Has he found out his calling?
Photo: AdobeStock l 圖片:Adobe Stock
註：find out 通常指經探索或觀察而發現某些資訊，例如：to find out the truth, to find out how to do something 等。找到失去的錢包、找到追求的目標之類，一般會用 to find。
2. 我擔心得睡不著覺。
ˇ I was too worried to go to sleep.
χ I was too worried to go to bed.
註：to go to bed 是「就寢」、「上床」；本句中的 to go to sleep 是 「睡著」、「入睡」，兩者不可相混。
3. 他從不向程度好的同學請教學習。
ˇ He never learns from the better students.
χ He never studies from the better students.
註：「向某人學習」是 to learn (something) from（或 of），不是 to study from。
4. 我從他那得知王先生幾個月前去世了。
ˇ I learned from him that Mr. Wang had passed away a few months ago.
χ I knew from him that Mr. Wang had passed away a few months ago.
註：to learn from someone 表示「從某人那聽來」、「從某人那得悉」，不可以說 to know from someone。又to learn from someone 也可作「向某人學習……」解。參上例。
5. 我和她相識已經很久了。
ˇ I have known her for a long time.
ˇ I met her a long time ago.
ˇ I got acquainted with her a long time ago.
χ I have recognized her a long time .
註：recognize 是「認出」、「看出」，意為「見了某人而認識」，是瞬間動詞，不可與表示持續時間的副詞連用。
to know、to get acquainted with 或 to make one’s acquaintance 是「與…相識」。
Exercises:
A. 她和我哥哥相識已經很久了。
She has __________ my older brother for a long time.
1. recognized
2. known
3. acquainted
4. understood
B. 她父親從電視上得知他女兒大賽獲勝的消息。
Her father __________ his daughter’s title victory on TV.
1. know
3. learn of
4. learned of
Answers: A. 2 B. 4
文章由書林出版公司提供：
www.bookman.com.tw
蘇正隆 — 台灣翻譯學學會前理事長、師大翻譯研究所兼任副教授; 編著《走讀自然.花言樹語》，《英語的對與錯》，《世紀病毒：必讀防疫英文知識與詞彙》...等。國家教育研究院中英雙語詞彙審議委員；研究領域為翻譯、術語及詞典編譯，從事植物與人文導覽數十年，亦曾應邀遠赴國外大學做植物人文導覽。

Zelenskiy rejects wartime elections call
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:45 UTC
01:38:45 KST

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said in remarks made public yesterday that it would be too dangerous for Ukraine to hold an election while it fights Russia’s invasion, after a call by his former defense minister to organize a vote.
Ukraine has suspended elections under martial law, a measure widely supported by the population as the country focuses on fighting off the Russian invasion launched in 2022.
“I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk. Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine,” Zelenskiy said.
Photo: AFP
“If we want to destroy the country, then we can move in the direction of elections during these times of war,” added the 48-year-old, who became president in 2019.
He made the comments on Saturday in a briefing with journalists, the first in months amid several political crises.
The latest upheaval saw thousands of people take to the streets after Zelenskiy fired popular former Ukrainian minister of defense Mykhailo Fedorov.
The ousted Fedorov this week made a surprise call to find a way to organize elections — but without offering a road map, and prompting even some of his supporters to distance themselves from him.
Experts have cited a flurry of obstacles to elections, including how soldiers, millions of Ukrainian refugees and people from occupied territories would vote, as well as disinformation threats from Russia.
The election call also came as Ukraine struggles to fend off daily Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and other cities.
Only 15 percent of Ukrainians believe elections should be held before the end of hostilities, a poll by the Kyiv Institute of Sociology showed.
Meanwhile, France on Saturday promised to deliver new interceptor missiles to Ukraine amid a surge in Russian strikes that have pushed civilian deaths in the four-and-a-half-year war to their highest since the first months of Moscow’s invasion.
At least 13 people were killed in strikes overnight and through Saturday — seven in Ukraine, four in Russia and two in Russia-annexed Crimea.
The latest deadly attacks come as rescuers in the eastern Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rig were sifting through the rubble of a partly destroyed shopping center, where 16 were killed a day earlier in a Russian drone attack.
Ukraine’s allies in the Coalition of the Willing — an initiative led by France and the UK — were today to meet to look at how to ramp up pressure on Moscow to halt its invasion.
“It is crucial to provide Ukraine with all the necessary means to defend its skies and thwart this aggression,” French President Emmanuel Macron wrote on X.
Russia has pounded Ukraine — the Kyiv especially — with ballistic missile attacks in the past few months.
The hard-to-intercept weapons reach their target within minutes, making it virtually impossible for locals in Kyiv to reach an underground shelter in time.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said in comments published on Saturday that Kyiv had opened “Pandora’s box” with its strikes on Russian economic targets, saying that Russia would hit back at Ukraine’s “most sensitive economic sectors.”
Ukraine has this summer escalated a campaign of drone strikes targeting Russian economic infrastructure, including oil refineries and online retailers’ warehouses, seeking to destroy infrastructure it says is central to Russia’s war effort.
Russia has responded with strikes against Ukrainian economic infrastructure, including Ukrainian grain exports via the Black Sea.
“The Kyiv regime set out to damage our economy. What did it do? It opened this Pandora’s box itself. Well then, expect a response targeting your most sensitive economic sectors,” Putin said in comments to a Russian state television journalist.
Additional reporting by Reuters

Taiwan needs balanced income distribution: expert
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:45 UTC
01:38:45 KST

With GDP per capita forecast to rise to about US$45,000 this year and approach US$50,000 next year amid the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, how to ensure a more balanced distribution of income is becoming a concern, an economist said.
Although GDP per capita is rising rapidly, the benefits of strong exports driven by robust global demand for AI-related products have been concentrated in the information and communications technology sector, raising concerns about a “K-shaped” economic recovery.
K-shaped growth refers to a divergence in the performance of different sectors, with some moving higher while others decline, creating a pattern resembling the arms of the letter “K.”
Photo: Ritchie B. Tongo, EPA
Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research (CIER) president Lien Hsien-ming (連賢明) is among the economists concerned about unbalanced economic development, as GDP is forecast to grow 11.05 percent this year and expand 6.04 percent next year.
The government should allocate more funds to social welfare programs, including labor insurance, civil servant insurance and national health insurance, to bolster their financial foundations, Lien said in an interview with CNA.
Injecting public funds into social welfare programs could improve wealth distribution and create long-term benefits for social equality and economic stability, Lien added.
“Fund allocations to social welfare will be a long-term task,” he said. “Although such efforts are unlikely to produce immediate effects, they are a must.”
Last week, President William Lai (賴清德) announced that the government would include NT$235.7 billion (US$7.40 billion) in its proposed central government budget for next year to fund a universal NT$10,000 cash handout so that “the AI dividend can be shared by all.”
Lien said the cash handout could be an effective way to put some of those benefits directly into people’s pockets, but improving social welfare would be a better approach to providing greater support for low-income families.
People with low income find it difficult to share in the benefits of Taiwan’s AI-driven economic growth, Lien said.
Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics Department of Statistics head Tsai Yu-tai (蔡鈺泰) said Taiwanese manufacturers took advantage of trade tensions between the US and China, the global supply chain realignment during the COVID-19 pandemic and the surge in AI demand, which helped boost Taiwan’s income.
However, fluctuations in the New Taiwan dollar against the US dollar could affect GDP per capita calculations, Tsai said.
If the NT dollar depreciates against the greenback, GDP per capita measured in US dollars would fall, and vice versa, he said.
The agency’s GDP per capita estimate for next year was based on an exchange rate of about NT$32.35 per US$1.

Research center develops new black soybean cultivar
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:45 UTC
01:38:45 KST

The Hualien District Agricultural Research and Extension Station has developed the “Lanyang No. 1” black soybean, which is expected to boost black soybean production due to its lodging resistance and consistent ripening stage.
The Lanyang No. 1 cultivar was selectively bred and developed from heirloom black soybean seeds from Yilan County — a small yellow-kernel black soybean variety that has been passed down locally for more than 50 years, the station said.
Yilan’s heirloom black soybean is a traditional ingredient in locally brewed soy sauce or fermented tofu, it said.
Photo courtesy of the Hualien District Agricultural Research and Extension Station
However, genotypes of such heirloom varieties are complex, leading to varying ripening stages and a higher plant lodging rate in field cultivation, the station said.
That constituted a major challenge for local black soybean growers in shifting to mechanized farming and field management, it said, adding that Lanyang No. 1 overcame the challenge.
Lanyang No. 1 exhibits a semi-indeterminate growth pattern with many branches and pods and long internodes, the station said.
It is also characterized by its white flowers, making it distinctive from most other black soybean cultivars in Taiwan, the station said, adding that the cultivar’s 100-grain weight ranges from 12g to 15g.
Under organic spring cropping, the average production of Lanyang No. 1 in eastern Taiwan reached 1.5 tonnes per hectare, it said.
Gee Young Farm director Wu Ching-chung (吳慶鐘), who participated in the collaborative research done by the station, said he is confident that Lanyang No. 1 would facilitate mass production of black soybeans.
Lanyang No. 1 had more consistent growth patterns, making it easier to manage the crop in fields with greater production, he said.
The station said it would continue to promote the cultivation techniques of Lanyang No. 1 and assist local growers in resolving potential difficulties.

A 39-year-old Taiwanese woman has been arrested on arrival at Japan’s Kansai International Airport on Saturday on suspicion of splashing a liquid on a national treasure housed in a temple in Nara when she visited it in April, Japanese media reported. She was arrested on suspicion of violating Japan’s Act on Protection of Cultural Properties.
The media reports said the woman, surnamed Tsai (蔡), allegedly splashed glycerin on the Buddha’s Footprint Stone, a national treasure displayed in the World Heritage-listed Yakushiji Temple in Japan’s Nara Prefecture, when she visited it on April 6.
Temple staff called the police when they found traces of the liquid on the stone, and the police identified Tsai from security camera footage, the reports said.
Photo: Sreen grab from the temple's Website
During police questioning, Tsai was quoted as admitting to the act by saying “I pour oil and pray over things that move me, so I may have poured oil on the Buddha’s Footstone,” the reports said, adding that she told the police that she had performed similar acts at other locations in Japan in the past.
Nara police are investigating whether other cultural properties or temple grounds have been damaged.
The details reported by Japanese media have been speculated by Taiwanese netizens to match those of Taiwanese entertainer Tsai Yi-chen (蔡宜臻), who goes by the stage name Wu-hsiung (五熊).
Her agent had not responded to messages seeking comment as of press time.
The Buddha’s Footprint Stone is a monument carved with what is said to be the footprint of Shakyamuni Buddha, with immense historical, religious and cultural value.
Inscribed with the era name Tenpyo-shoho Year 5 (753 AD), the stone in Yakushiji Temple is the oldest among approximately 300 Buddha’s Footstones available for viewing across Japan.

Indonesian migrant fishers launch campaign for workers’ rights
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:42 UTC
01:38:42 KST

Indonesian migrant fishers yesterday launched the “Freedom for Fishers Campaign” at Donggang Fishing Harbor in Pingtung County, alongside celebrations marking Indonesia’s 81st Independence Day on Aug. 17.
After attendees sang the Indonesian national anthem, the Forum Silaturahmi Pelaut Indonesia-Pingtung County Migrant Fishers Union (FOPSI-PMFU) announced the campaign’s demands, including fair wages and employment contracts and guaranteed access to Wi-Fi on all vessels.
They also appealed for the right to organize and join a union free from intimidation and retaliation, a transparent and fair grievance mechanism, and healthy and safe working conditions.
Photo: CNA
In a speech, FOPSI-PMFU Chairman Rojani told the nearly 100 attendees that Indonesia’s Independence Day is a day of pride and solidarity for Indonesians.
For migrant fishers, however, independence means more than being able to raise their national flag. It also means being able to live and work with dignity, speak without fear, and be free from forced labor, exploitation, intimidation and retaliation, he said.
Taiwan’s government has repeatedly insisted that many of these issues have been addressed and improved, but the US Department of Labor put Taiwan on its biennial “List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor” in 2021 and is still on the list today.
FOPSI-PMFU Secretary-General Achmad Mudzakir said the abuses continue, with the union recently receiving a report from a fisher who said he had been subjected to violence while working on a distant-water fishing vessel.
After the union reported the incident to the Fisheries Agency, however, the broker and employer fired and repatriated the fisher after learning of the complaint, without allowing time for reporting and response procedures to be completed, Mudzakir said.
Regarding infrastructure at Donggang harbor, Mudzakir said there were only two bathrooms on shore, each with about five stalls, for some 4,500 fishers working aboard offshore and distant-water fishing vessels in the area, which he said was far from sufficient.
He also called for Wi-Fi hotspots to be installed in the harbor so fishers aboard distant-water vessels can access the internet when they return to shore.
Through the campaign, the union hopes to reach a binding and implementable agreement with companies in the international seafood supply chain to better protect the rights of migrant fishers.
Migrant fishers are at the bottom of the supply chain, the union said, but meaningful change can only take place when companies and brands at the top of the supply chain take appropriate responsibility.

KMT head touts rapport at 823 memorial
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:41 UTC
01:38:41 KST

Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun (鄭麗文) yesterday called on President William Lai (賴清德) to recognize the so-called “1992 consensus” to ease cross-strait tensions.
The “1992 consensus” refers to a tacit understanding between the KMT and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) that both sides of the Strait acknowledge there is “one China,” with each side having its own interpretation of what “China” means. The Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) has never acknowledged the “1992 consensus,” saying that Beijing does not recognize the ROC and acceptance of the understanding would imply agreement with China’s territorial claim over Taiwan.
Cheng made the remarks during a visit to the 823 Artillery Bombardment Museum in Kinmen to mark the 68th anniversary of the battle.
Photo courtesy of the KMT
The 823 Artillery Bombardment refers to the engagement that began on Aug. 23, 1958. China launched an offensive, firing more than 470,000 artillery shells in the bombardment of Kinmen over 44 days. Communist forces failed to capture the islands, marking a victory for the Republic of China (ROC) administration in Taiwan. Soldiers killed during the battle defended the ROC and the values of ROC Constitution, including democracy, freedom, equitable prosperity and the people’s right to live with dignity and affluence, Cheng said.
Commemorating the battle today means continuing to uphold and safeguard the values of the ROC Constitution, she said. This generation is responsible for “creating peace,” she said, saying that the KMT wants to start from Kinmen and pledge a century of peace, transforming the island from a military stronghold into a hub for peace.
If Lai would recognize the “1992 consensus,” the two sides of the Taiwan Strait could resume contact, dialogue and exchanges, reducing tensions, she said.
Cheng yesterday said that if Lai believes Taiwanese independence is not a real issue, he should shelve the DPP’s advocacy for Taiwanese independence rather than seeking to replace the ROC Constitution through constitution-drafting, nation-building or independence initiatives.
An official familiar with cross-strait affairs, speaking on condition of anonymity, said in response to Cheng’s claims that the “1992 consensus” leaves no room for the ROC.
“Only people who have lost their senses would help the CCP eliminate the ROC and annex Taiwan,” they said.
Asking Lai to accept the “1992 consensus” is asking him to eliminate his own country, they said, calling it a “massive joke.”
Cheng should first ask Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) to recognize the ROC and give it room to exist, they said. The August 23 Artillery Battle was fought to defend the ROC, they said, accusing Cheng of parroting Beijing’s goal of eliminating Taiwan.
“Is it appropriate for the chair of the KMT to make such remarks at an event commemorating the 823 Artillery Bombardment?” the official asked. “Does that do justice to the soldiers and civilians who defended the nation at the time?”
The KMT has degenerated to such a degree that if former presidents Chiang Kai-shek (蔣介石) and Chiang Ching-kuo (蔣經國) were alive today, they wonder what they would think of what the party has become, the official said.

Ports integrating AI for sea safety, cargo management
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:41 UTC
01:38:41 KST

Taiwan International Ports Corp (TIPC) said it has completed the installation of a smart harbor-entrance safety monitoring system, using artificial intelligence (AI) to monitor vessel movements at commercial ports across the country.
The system enhances the commercial port operators’ water safety management capabilities by replacing traditional port patrols with a proactive warning mechanism.
Maritime and weather information from the Central Weather Administration are to integrate into the system, sharpening its capabilities to respond to disasters and emergencies.
Photo courtesy of Taiwan International Ports Corp
The Port of Kaohsiung has completed a proof of concept for an AI-powered occupational safety monitoring application for vessel loading and unloading operations, allowing them to identify risks in real time, it said.
The state-run commercial port operator has established an AI Promotion and Implementation Committee to ensure that all decisionmaking processes are driven by data.
Biofuel bunkering services would be launched at the Port of Kaohsiung during the second half of this year, it added, saying it is seeking operators to provide liquified natural gas (LNG) in line with CPC Corp, Taiwan’s schedule for completing and commencing gas supply from its LNG receiving terminal.
TIPC aims to have 16 high-voltage shore power terminals in commercial ports nationwide by the first quarter of next year by increasing such facilities in the ports of Kaohsiung and Keelung, it said. This would reduce carbon emissions while vessels are moored, it added.
The port corporation is planning to develop bunkering infrastructure for other zero-carbon fuels at ports around the country in the longer term, such as hydrogen, ammonia and green methanol in line with the Ministry of Transportation and Communications’ alternative maritime fuel initiatives.
The Port of Kaohsiung ranked 17th globally in last year’s Container Port Performance Index, published by the World Bank and S&P Global Market Intelligence, and ninth in the Norwegian Veritas’ global ranking of container ports last year, the port corporation said.
TIPC chairman Chou Yung-hui (周永暉) said the company remains cautiously optimistic for the cruise industry this year, despite the impact of Middle East conflicts, tariffs and typhoons on container and bulk cargo operations.
Company data showed that 332 international cruise ship stops were recorded at Taiwan’s ports in the first half of the year, bringing 628,600 passengers. The company predicts 605 stops for this year, while passenger numbers are expected to rise from 1.1567 million last year to more than 1.197 million, which would be a new record.
Keelung Port is expanding its homeport services and to draw more international cruise lines, with passenger numbers expected to exceed 1 million for the first time. Kaohsiung Port is developing homeport and port-of-call services to promote cruise tourism in southern Taiwan, the company said.

Photo: Reuters
Tamberi took several different approaches to his jumps, sometimes urging the crowd to clap along, at other times preferring silence, and when the Italian went with music, it ranged from classical to techno.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher

CPC Corp, Taiwan (CPC, 台灣中油) on Saturday announced that it would keep retail gasoline and diesel prices unchanged this week, while Formosa Petrochemical Corp (台塑石化) yesterday said it would maintain its fuel prices at the same levels despite a spike in international crude oil prices.
The decisions mark the fourth consecutive week that CPC and Formosa have kept domestic fuel prices unchanged, although crude oil prices moved higher last week after Iran vowed a “devastating” response to US threats to impose tighter economic sanctions.
CPC said its floating price mechanism, based on a weighted average of 70 percent Dubai and 30 percent Brent crude, showed that the average international crude oil price rose to US$93.01 last week from US$89.84 per barrel the previous week.
However, a stronger New Taiwan dollar, which averaged NT$31.901 against the US dollar last week, compared with NT$32.194 a week earlier, helped moderate the financial pressure from higher crude oil purchasing costs, CPC said.
Retail gasoline prices this week would remain at NT$30.5, NT$32 and NT$34 per liter for 92, 95 and 98-octane unleaded gasoline respectively at CPC and Formosa stations, while prices of premium diesel would stay at NT$29.3 per liter at CPC stations and NT$29.1 per liter at Formosa pumps, the companies said.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:22 UTC
01:38:22 KST

Organizers of this year’s Sydney Marathon have sparked online mirth by unveiling a finishers’ medal depicting a stadium in far-away Munich, Germany.
The two-sided medal is engraved with a Sydney skyline showing course landmarks including the Opera House, the Sydney Harbour Bridge — and the Allianz Arena in Munich.
Marathon bosses admitted the “unfortunate error” in the medal, which displays the German arena’s shape and diamond-patterned exterior instead of the flatter features of Allianz Stadium in Sydney.
Photo: EPA
“A little too much international flavor has found its way onto the back of the finishers medal, with an incorrect depiction of the stadium,” a Sydney Marathon spokesperson said. “We’re not going to run from it, it was an unfortunate error, though it’s certainly given everyone something to talk about this weekend, mostly in good humor.”
The medal’s reception on social media was light-hearted.
“Oh, dear. Oh, this is bad,” Instagram account @morningcoffeerun said, speculating that someone might have mixed up the stadiums in an online search for Allianz.
Munich’s Allianz Arena treated the medal muddle with good humor.
“Oh wow, we didn’t have that on our bingo card!” it posted on Instagram. “Perhaps they tried to find something else they had in common: Allianz Arena — Sydney Opera — Unique Architecture — Both are worth a visit!”
Australian media also had fun with the slip.
“The medal that will put Sydney on the map. The wrong map,” ran a headline in the Sydney Morning Herald.
The other side of the Sydney Marathon medal shows a widely praised blue-and-gold design by indigenous artist Ambrose Killian, who said he was not involved in the creation of the Sydney skyline.
Marathon organizers said they expect a record of more than 40,000 participants who would earn the medal as a “badge of honor” for completing the 42.2km course.
“With the event a week away, this is the medal our finishers will receive,” the Sydney Marathon spokesperson said.
“Behind every one of these medals is months of early mornings, long runs and quiet determination, and having it placed around your neck at the Sydney Opera House is a moment our participants will never forget,” the spokesperson added. “It’s a beautiful medal, and now a little more unique.”

Taiwan must uphold spirit of 823: Lai
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:22 UTC
01:38:22 KST

Even in peacetime, forgetting war is dangerous, but Taiwan will uphold the spirit of those who were on the front lines of the Second Taiwan Strait Crisis and not cede an inch of territory, President William Lai (賴清德) said in Kinmen County yesterday during an event marking the 68th anniversary of the 823 Artillery Bombardment.
At the rain-soaked event, to commemorate the Aug. 23, 1958, Chinese attack on Kinmen that started the Second Taiwan Strait Crisis, Lai expressed his respect and gratitude to the soldiers who, regardless of their backgrounds, united and fought to defend Taiwan proper and Kinmen, Penghu and Lienchiang counties.
Over 44 days, more than 470,000 artillery shells were fired at Kinmen, killing 456 military personnel and 162 civilians, and wounding 1,972 military personnel and 638 civilians. The defense of the islands is regarded as a significant battle that helped safeguard the Republic of China government in Taiwan.
Photo: Chiang Ying-ying, AP
The victory laid an important foundation for 68 years of peace across the Taiwan Strait and thwarted China’s ambitions to expand its aggression toward the First Island Chain and elsewhere in the Indo-Pacific region, Lai said.
“China has never abandoned its ambitions for expansion over the past 68 years,” he said. “Today, in addition to its increasingly aggressive ‘gray zone’ incursions into waters around waters near Kinmen through its coast guard, China’s military has expanded its provocations from Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu, to the First Island Chain and the Indo-Pacific region, threatening not only peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait, but also creating unease among Indo-Pacific nations.”
Peace is hard-won, but a peace agreement that sacrifices the nation’s sovereignty and entails submission to would not result in genuine peace, he said.
Photo: Ritchie B. Tongo, EPA
The government’s defense budget for next year would exceed NT$1 trillion (US$31.4 billion) for the first time, reaching NT$1.12 trillion and remaining above 3 percent of GDP, the president said, adding that the spending demonstrates Taiwan’s commitment to bolstering its self-defense capabilities.
In addition to enhancing military capabilities, the government has continued to improve compensation for military personnel, Lai said.
Since last year, the government has increased the volunteer military, combat unit, air and control, signals intelligence and cyberwarfare allowances. In February, drone units were also made eligible for the combat-unit allowance.
Starting last month, a third category of combat-unit allowance was introduced based on operational requirements and the nature of duties, providing an additional NT$4,000 per month. Conscripts serving in combat units are also eligible for the allowance.
Professional and supervisory allowances for military personnel, civil servants and public school teachers were each increased by NT$2,000, while salaries are to rise by 4 percent across the board beginning in January next year.
The increase next year would be the fifth pay raise for military, civil servants and public school teachers over the past decade, demonstrating the government’s support for those groups, Lai said.
All of the government’s efforts are aimed at providing greater defense resources and better benefits to support every service member who helps defend the country, he said.
“If Taiwan was able to prevail 68 years ago, despite difficult circumstances, by uniting civilians and the military and defeating a larger force, then today, 68 years later, people should be even more united in supporting the armed forces and national defense,” he said.

Students victim to sex scams: bureau
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-23
16:38:21 UTC
01:38:21 KST

More than 350 students fell victim to sex-service scams over summer vacation, with one college student losing NT$300,000, the Criminal Investigation Bureau said yesterday, urging people who encounter such scams or coercion to report them.
Arranging or soliciting paid sexual encounters, including transactions disguised as casual meetings, is illegal, the bureau said in a news release yesterday, adding that meetings arranged through online platforms have become increasingly more common.
People caught engaging in such activities can face detention or fines under the Social Order Maintenance Act (社會秩序維護法), while also being exposed to potential fraud and personal safety risks, the bureau said.
Photo: CNA
Sex scams have consistently ranked among the top five scams on the 165 Anti-Fraud Dashboard, it said.
Its data showed that 356 students fell victim to such scams during summer vacation, losing from NT$2,000 to NT$300,000, the bureau said.
One 21-year-old college student from southern Taiwan started chatting with a woman who posted on the social media platform Threads saying that she was a third-year student hoping to connect with other students.
The woman then claimed her family had fallen on hard times and offered part-time escort services, with the two agreeing on NT$3,000 for an encounter.
She then told the student to buy NT$3,000 in game credits at a nearby convenience store to avoid a cash transaction, before demanding another NT$5,000 in credits and a photo of his ID to prove he was not an undercover police officer
The student provided the card numbers, passwords and a photo of his ID, but the woman then demanded more than NT$10,000 in game credits as “dating gifts” and a “meeting fee.”
When he hesitated, a man claiming to be a gang member demanded another NT$50,000 and threatened him and his family, claiming his identity verification had failed.
The student borrowed money from his family, but after handing over a total of NT$300,000 and unable to pay more, he reported the case to police and realized he had been scammed.
These scammers use social media and adult Web sites to offer fake escort services, the bureau said.
After gaining victims’ trust, they demand game credits for supposed deposits or security fees, then redeem the credits using the card numbers and passwords, it said.
Once game card numbers and passwords are given to scammers, the credits can be transferred to third-party accounts or used in online transactions, making the funds difficult for police to trace and victims to recover, the bureau said.
Scammers also exploit victims’ eagerness to complete the deal and reluctance to tell others, repeatedly pressuring them to buy more credits, it added.
The bureau urged people who encounter scams or coercion while meeting people online to call 110 or 165 to report it to police.

Photo: Reuters

Anthropic declined AFP’s request for comment.

Anthropic’s commercial success has been accompanied by difficulties in meeting demand for computing power, amid a shortage of chips and servers.

Salek is joining the compute team of Anthropic, the company said.
The executive ran Google’s tensor processing unit business until 2022 and delivered the first seven generations of those chips.
After leaving Google, Salek has been senior managing director at Cerberus Capital Management LP. He also previously worked at Nvidia.
Anthropic, which buys chips from a variety of sources, has indicated that it wants to build an in-house silicon business.
Like other AI giants, Anthropic is scrambling to get enough data center infrastructure to support its ambitions. Custom chips would potentially help it cope with supply shortages and tailor designs to better meet its needs.
